threads.body: The deprecation warning emitted here is always phrased as a deprecated *system property*, but `enabled` may have come from deprecated declarative config (`java.messaging.receive_telemetry/...`) via `config.getBoolean(...)` (even when `systemPropertyFallback` is false). This can mislead users who aren’t using system properties. Consider splitting the read path so you can detect the source (declarative vs system property) and emit an accurate warning message (e.g., ‘setting and equivalent declarative property are deprecated’ when the declarative value is present, and ‘system property is deprecated’ only when the value comes from `SystemProperty`).

Downsides: The warning is slightly longer for users who supplied only a flat property.

threads.body: These tests attach a `java.util.logging.Handler` to a global logger. If the test suite runs in parallel, other tests executing `MessagingConfig` can emit warnings during this window, causing `handler.records` assertions to become flaky. To harden this, consider filtering captured log records to only those matching the specific deprecated key under test (e.g., implement a `Filter` or only add records when the message contains `warning-test`), or otherwise isolating logging so unrelated warnings don’t affect the record count.

Addressed in 3ac18d3bf20b92c1a0f95463c177e4e389157eb9.

Analysis: The renamed-selector overload passed the replacement `.included` property to both consumers. The deprecation warning therefore omitted the valid `.excluded` replacement, while wildcard guidance correctly needs the narrower `.included` target. The messaging caller also represented the replacement namespace once as a literal and again inside the flat-property prefix. The overload now derives the full selector property pair for deprecation warnings, and MessagingConfig derives its flat-property prefix from one namespace constant.

Upsides: Deprecation warnings list both supported replacement properties. Wildcard warnings still point to `.included`. The messaging namespace now has one source of truth, and a focused test protects the warning text.

Downsides: The new constant and test add a small amount of code. No material runtime downside identified.

threads.body: The selector-level early return breaks replacement-first aliasing for mixed migrations. For example, if the new `included=*` property is set while the deprecated `excluded=authorization` property remains, the non-empty new selector returns here and silently drops the exclusion, potentially capturing a sensitive header. Resolve `included` and `excluded` independently—use each canonical leaf when present, otherwise fall back to its matching deprecated leaf—and build the selector only after both leaves are resolved.

replies.body:
Addressed in 7991add0c20376a12ce8c11322d66e8a2689fc9a.

Analysis: MessagingConfig returned as soon as either canonical header leaf made a non-empty selector. This skipped the deprecated selector node, so a canonical included list could discard a deprecated excluded list. Resolving each leaf before building IncludeExclude preserves replacement-first precedence for each property.

Upsides: Mixed migrations retain exclusions and avoid capturing headers that the deprecated excluded list still protects.

Downsides: The resolver now reads both header nodes before it builds the selector. No material runtime cost is expected.
